name: Built-in widgets

A rich-text note with a formatting toolbar. Edits save on their own about half a second after you stop typing.

## What it can show

- Headings, like the two above
- A bulleted list, like this one

name: Demo providers
description: One card per data provider that answers on the openbq-docker v3 stack without a sign-up of your own. BLS, CFTC, EconDB and Nasdaq need no key; EIA and Congress.gov use the providers' public demo keys from credentials.demo.env, and a key of your own in credentials.env takes their place. Demo keys are rate-limited, so answers can vary between runs. Opens in BDOBB 3.0.0 or later.

name: OpenBB Workspace - BLS

The two Parameter echo cards below share a Ticker group: the chain-link beside each card's Ticker control opens the Groups menu, the numbered badge shows which group a control is in, and editing either card's Ticker moves both.

Each card below resolves one date expression against today and the XNYS exchange calendar, so its dates move with the calendar. Top row: T (today), T-5bd (five business days back), T-1m (one calendar month back). Bottom row: M-1 (start of last month), FQ-4 (start of the fiscal quarter four back), Y-1 (start of last year).

name: Parameters
description: The v4 parameter features on their own tabs: groups that propagate one value to many cards, the period-aware pickers (day, week, month, quarter, fiscal year, date-time and time) and the relative-date grammar. Every card is a built-in that echoes what it would send, so nothing needs a backend, a key or a sign-up. Opens in BDOBB 4.0.0 or later.

params.text: The two Parameter echo cards below share two groups: Symbol (on each card's Ticker) and Year. The chain-link beside a control opens the Groups menu, the numbered badge shows which group a control is in, and editing either card's Ticker -- or its Year -- moves both. Groups are per dashboard; a group here never touches another dashboard.

Each Period echo card carries one control of every kind -- day, week, month, quarter, fiscal year, date-time (to the second) and time -- so a fiscal-quarter parameter picks a quarter, not a day on a calendar. The two cards share a Quarter group but end their fiscal years in different months: the same stored quarter shows two different labels, which is exactly what the fiscal-quarter alignment fixes.

A date parameter can store an expression instead of a frozen date, and every render resolves it fresh -- so a dashboard set up on "26 weeks ago" keeps meaning 26 weeks ago, not the day it was built. Each Date expression card below types one expression and shows what it resolves to today, as a date and as a datetime. Edit the Expression control to try your own; the fiscal cards read their year end from the FY end control.

name: Example Dashboard - Version 6.0.0
description: The v6.0.0 Rita stage: a small board Rita can see and rearrange for you. Set the Rita URL and turn on Context sharing in AI Library ▸ Agents so Rita can see these cards, then ask it to work the board — "add a note summarising the day", "rename this dashboard to Markets". Every widget is a built-in, so no backend is needed. Rita arrived in 6.0.0, so this needs BDOBB 6.0.0 or later.

params.text:
# Rita can work this board

With **Context Sharing** on (AI Library ▸ Agents), Rita sees every card here and can author the dashboard for you. Try asking it to:

- **Add a note** — "add a note summarising today's session" (Rita writes a markdown card).
- **Rename** — "rename this dashboard to Markets", or "call the clock card World Clock".
- **Rearrange** — "move the clock to the top", "make this note full width".
- **Add a tab** — "add a Rates tab".
- **Add a widget** — "add a clock" (Rita finds it with search_widgets, then adds it).

Rita only sees the board while Context Sharing is on, and never sees a Keys widget. Everything it does is one **Undo** away.

## Scratch
A plain note for Rita to rename, move, or replace. Ask it: "tidy this board."

name: Example Dashboard - Version 7.0.0
description: The v7.0.0 iPad touch showcase: three built-in widgets, each with a touch gesture to try. The Note lists the gestures, including tapping the left rail to open it and tapping outside to close it. The Clock reflows; the long Markdown card scrolls with a one-finger drag and zooms with a two-finger pinch. Every widget is a built-in, so no backend is needed. Opens in BDOBB 7.0.0 or later.

params.text:
## Try these gestures
- **No mouse?** Tap the left rail to open it, and tap anywhere outside it to close. With a trackpad or Magic Keyboard it opens on hover, like on desktop.
- **Two-finger pinch** anywhere to zoom.
- **Drag** inside the Markdown card to scroll it.
- **Tap** a card's ⋯ for its menu (with widget controls collapsed, tap the ⌄ first).
- **Double-tap** a card header's empty background, or tap ⤢, to maximize, and again to restore. Double-tapping the title renames the card.
- Tap into this note and type — the pane must not collapse while focused.

name: Example Dashboard - Version 8.0.0 - Pinned Cards
description: The v8.0.0 pinned cards: a Note pinned to the top of the tab and a Clock to the bottom, with a long Markdown card between them that scrolls while the bands stay put and walks through Pin widget ▸. The pins travel in BDOBB's v8 extension, so this file opens in BDOBB 8.0.0 or later. Every widget is a built-in, and the file carries no locked widgets, which would replace your own.

params.text:
## Pinned cards

This Note is **pinned to the top** of the tab and the Clock to the **bottom**. Scroll the tab: the Markdown card between them moves, and the two bands stay put.

On any card, **⋯ ▸ Pin widget ▸** has **Pin to top**, **Pin to bottom** and **Unpin**. Drag a band's corner grips to make it taller or shorter. One card per edge per tab: pinning a second swaps the first back into the grid.

# Scroll me

This long card sits in the grid between the two pinned bands. Scroll the tab and it moves while the Note above and the Clock below stay in view.

## Try

1. Open this card's **⋯** menu and choose **Pin widget ▸ Pin to top**. It swaps places with the Note, which goes back into the grid.
2. Choose **Unpin** on it to put it back where it was.
3. **Maximize** a pinned card: it covers the bands, and **Escape** puts it back.

## Where a pin travels

A pin is saved with the dashboard and syncs with it. **Save…** in the **BDOBB Workspace** format carries it in BDOBB's v8 extension, which is why this file needs BDOBB 8.0.0 or later. **Duplicate** and **Copy to** never copy a pin.

## Locked widgets are different

A widget along an edge of every dashboard is *locked*, not pinned, and is set up in **Settings ▸ Locked Widgets**. This example carries none: importing locked widgets replaces your own.
